text:
ChatJS

 The building blocks for your AI app. 

Start with a working AI chat. Choose your models and tools. Own the code.

 Create an app · Try the demo · Read the docs 

 

 ChatJS 1.0 is in alpha. Use chat-js@alpha to try it. APIs, configuration, and generated code may change before the stable release.

 Quickstart

Use Node.js 24 or newer. You can scaffold interactively from the terminal. The browser builder lets you preview the UI, configure the agent, and copy a tailored command. Open the builder

 

The CLI asks which gateway, authentication providers, and optional features to include. Fill in .env.local with your PostgreSQL connection, gateway and authentication credentials, and any settings required by your selections. Generate AUTH SECRET and EVE GATEWAY SECRET separately with openssl rand -base64 32 . Full setup guide

 

The setup command applies app migrations and prepares EVE's workflow database. Open localhost:3000 to sign in and send your first message.

 What you get

- A working chat app. Next.js, TypeScript, and shadcn/ui with streaming responses, saved conversations, and Better Auth. Scaffold with Base UI or Radix.
- A durable agent runtime. EVE runs conversations and tools, persists execution state, handles approvals, and lets the client reconnect to an in-progress response. Architecture
- Your choice of models. Use Vercel AI Gateway, OpenRouter, OpenAI, LiteLLM, or an OpenAI-compatible endpoint. Gateways
- Optional capabilities. Add uploads, projects, and sharing, or equip the agent with web search, code execution, image generation, or MCP connectors. Tools · Plugins

 Make it yours

Change branding, model defaults, and app settings in chat.config.ts . Customize agent behavior in agent/agent.ts . Tools and plugins are installed as source files you can edit and commit with your app. Source ownership

To add MCP connectors, run this from inside your app.

 

Generate MCP ENCRYPTION KEY with openssl rand -base64 32 and set it in .env.local . Run npm run db:generate , review the generated SQL, then apply it with npm run db:migrate . MCP setup · CLI reference

Deploy the web app on Vercel or self-host it with Docker or Node.js. Add the Electron companion to package your app for macOS, Windows, and Linux. Deployment guides · Desktop guide

 Contributing

This repository contains the reference app, site and builder, docs, Electron companion, CLI, and source registry.

For a fresh checkout, use Node.js 24+ and Bun from the repository root.

 

Use bun dev:info to find your local app URLs and bun dev:docs to work on the docs. For unattended local development on macOS, bun dev:service start registers supervision at login. Use bun dev:health to check readiness and bun dev:service stop to unregister it.

For registry changes, edit packages/registry/src and the relevant manifests. The development server mirrors them into apps/chat . Run bun lint , bun test:types , and the relevant tests before opening a PR. Repository instructions · Registry development · Release process

install.html:
Use Node.js 24 or newer. You can scaffold interactively from the terminal. The browser builder lets you preview the UI, configure the agent, and copy a tailored command. Open the builder

npx chat-js@alpha create my-app
cd my-app
cp .env.example .env.local

The CLI asks which gateway, authentication providers, and optional features to include. Fill in .env.local with your PostgreSQL connection, gateway and authentication credentials, and any settings required by your selections. Generate AUTH_SECRET and EVE_GATEWAY_SECRET separately with openssl rand -base64 32. Full setup guide

npm run setup
npm run dev

The setup command applies app migrations and prepares EVE's workflow database. Open localhost:3000 to sign in and send your first message.
